normalized.governing_thought: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, but fund it in stages: it is the only route within the board’s limits, and its payback depends on holding ad costs near pilot levels
executive_summary: WHETHER: Yes: the US deserves 2027’s single launch slot
US K-beauty skincare grew 17% a year to $3.6B (2021–25), against 5% for all facial skincare; 41% of it sells on Amazon.
The Amazon pilot sold 64,800 units in six months; monthly volume rose 89%, at 4.5 stars and 29% repeat (benchmark 31%).
A Japan scale-up is safer (+$1.8M cash by 2030) but adds only $7M of revenue in a market growing 1.5% a year.
ROUTE: Amazon-led (A) is the only route that fits the board’s limits
On planning inputs A needs at most $1.9M of cash, pays back in 2030 (+$2.4M) and keeps group margin at or above 9.5%.

Retail-led (B) breaches all three limits on its own inputs: −$20.8M peak cash (cap $18M), no payback, 4.5% group margin in 2027. Its inputs are also optimistic: 4.5 units/door/week vs 2.6 at Onsoo’s awareness.
No route reaches $40M by 2030 within the limits; A reaches $26M, and about $40M by 2032 if it keeps growing ~29% a year.
HOW: Payback hinges on ad cost, so commit in gated stages
A pays back by 2030 only if ACoS averages ≤28.6%; the pilot ran at 28%, but brands scaling to $5–20M run at a 32% median (→ −$2.3M in 2030).
The downside is bounded: across ten cases, peak cash stays ≤$7.2M (40% of the cap) and group margin ≥8.8%.
Gate spend on H2-2027 ad cost; treat specialty retail as an option to earn (≥20% awareness, door test ≥4.0 units/week), not a 2029 date.

Board decisions for March 2027: approve Stage 1 of Option A (2027 cash need $1.9–2.9M) · adopt ad-cost gates · pre-agree whether a 1–2-year payback slip is acceptable · restate the $40M ambition · raise the retail trigger

claims.claim: Should Onsoo enter the US market in 2027, and if so, by which route?
evidence: Recommendation for CEO Park Ji-won and the Board · March 2027 board meeting
Draft for discussion · prepared November 2026
All figures come from the US-entry briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data). $ = US dollars; KRW 1,380 per $.

slides.title: We tested the CEO’s Amazon-first hypothesis against four conditions: two hold, one holds only if ad costs stay low, and the retail trigger does not hold

claims.claim: Starting hypothesis (CEO): “Launch in the US in 2027 through Amazon, then add specialty beauty retail from 2029 once Amazon sales pass $10M and aided awareness passes 15%.”
1 The US is a better use of the single 2027 launch slot than a Japan scale-up — ✓ Holds
evidence: US K-beauty skincare +17% a year vs Japan +1.5%; pilot demand is real. Japan yields more 4-year cash (+$1.8M) but only $7M revenue and no US progress

claims.claim: 2 Amazon-led beats retail-led on the board’s limits — ✓ Holds
evidence: B breaches cap, payback and margin floor even on its own inputs; its sell-through and halo inputs are optimistic

claims.claim: 3 Amazon-led meets the cap, payback and margin limits under realistic inputs — ◐ Only if ad cost stays ≤28.6%
evidence: Cap and margin floor hold in all ten cases tested; payback by 2030 holds only if ACoS ≤28.6% (scale benchmark: 32%)

claims.claim: 4 Retail can be added profitably in 2029 at $10M Amazon sales and 15% awareness — ✗ Does not hold: raise to 20% and test first
evidence: At 10–20% awareness newcomers sell a median 3.5 units/door/week, below the 4.0 delisting line; retail fixed costs need ~4,250 doors to cover

claims.claim: Revised answer: enter the US in 2027 through Amazon (Option A), released in gated stages tied to ad cost at scale; keep specialty retail as an option earned at ≥20% awareness and a successful door test, not a dated 2029 commitment.
evidence: Board limits used throughout: peak cumulative US cash outflow ≤$18M through 2030 · cumulative US cash back to zero by end-2030 · group operating margin ≥8% every year · one major launch in 2027 · ambition “on the way to $40M by 2030”.

slides.title: US K-beauty skincare has grown 17% a year to $3.6B, over three times the category’s pace, and Amazon is where most of it is bought

claims.claim: US K-beauty skincare has grown 17% a year to $3.6B
evidence: US K-beauty facial skincare sales, $B: 2021 1.9, 2022 2.3, 2023 2.7, 2024 3.1, 2025 3.6
Share of all US facial skincare: 9.5%, 10.8%, 11.9%, 13.2%, 14.7%
The trade-press “$5.2B US K-beauty” figure also includes makeup and hair care, so we use the $3.6B skincare figure.

claims.claim: Amazon is where most of it is bought
evidence: Where US consumers bought K-beauty skincare, 2025: Amazon 41%, Specialty beauty retail 27%, Mass retail 14%, Brand websites (DTC) 12%, Other 6%

claims.claim: Survey: K-beauty buyers shop on Amazon and discover on TikTok
evidence: 61% buy K-beauty most often on Amazon; 22% at specialty beauty retail
38% discovered their last new brand on TikTok; 17% in a store
52% of K-beauty triers cite price vs US brands as a reason to buy
Source: September 2026 survey (n = 1,200 US women 18–44)

claims.claim: Onsoo is barely known
evidence: 4% aided awareness overall, 9% among K-beauty buyers

slides.title: The Amazon pilot shows real US demand: monthly sales nearly doubled in six months, at 4.5 stars and near-benchmark repeat

claims.claim: Monthly sales nearly doubled in six months
evidence: Pilot units sold per month, 2026 (thousand): Jan 7.4, Feb 8.6, Mar 10.1, Apr 11.8, May 12.9, Jun 14.0
64,800 units; $1.56M of sales in six months at $24.00 average price
+89% Jan → Jun monthly units (7,400 → 14,000), ≈ 14% a month compounded

claims.claim: 4.5 stars and near-benchmark repeat
evidence: 4.5 ★ from 2,140 reviews. Top complaint (6%): Korean-only labels, which US labelling in the 2027 setup budget fixes
29% repeat: 90-day repeat of first-time buyers vs 31% for first-year skincare brands on Amazon US (Onsoo Korea: 48%)

claims.claim: 300,000 is within reach, though it assumes new SKUs sell like the first three
evidence: June run-rate: 14,000 × 12 = 168,000 units a year from 3 SKUs, i.e. ~4,700 units per SKU per month.

claims.claim: 28% ACoS on a small ad budget: the number that must hold at scale
evidence: 28% ACoS

slides.title: A Japan scale-up is the safer use of 2027, but it adds only $7M of revenue by 2030 and does nothing for the US ambition

claims.claim: Japan scale-up is safer but adds only $7M of revenue
evidence: Market growth: Japan ~1.5% a year (Onsoo holds 3.1%); US K-beauty skincare 17% a year
Revenue added in 2030: J $7.0M; A@25% $26.4M; A@32% $26.4M
Operating profit 2030: J $1.3M; A@25% $3.1M; A@32% $1.2M
Cumulative cash end-2030: J +$1.8M; A@25% +$2.4M; A@32% −$2.3M
Peak cash need: J $1.1M; A@25% $1.9M; A@32% $3.2M
Lowest group operating margin: J 10.1%; A@25% 9.5%; A@32% 9.1%
Progress toward US $40M: J None; A $26.4M in 2030, still growing ~29% a year
Calculation (Japan, Table 7): contribution 30% × (2.5 + 4.5 + 6.0 + 7.0) = $6.0M, less fixed cost 4 × $0.8M and one-time $1.0M = +$1.8M

claims.claim: Japan yields more four-year cash than the US unless US ACoS stays below ~26%
evidence: 2030 revenue ~4× Japan’s, still growing ~29% a year

claims.claim: Use 2027 for the US. Waiting a year would not resolve the key unknown, ad cost at scale, which can only be learned by scaling in the US

slides.title: Per unit, retail earns more than Amazon ($7.55 vs $4.73), but its $7.5M a year of extra fixed cost would need ~4,250 doors to cover

claims.claim: Per unit, retail earns more than Amazon ($7.55 vs $4.73)
evidence: Rice Ferment Barrier Cream (50 ml), $ per unit: Price Onsoo receives Amazon 24.00 / Retail 14.00 (50% of $28 shelf)
Amazon referral fee (15%) −3.60 / —; FBA −5.10 / —; Advertising (ACoS 25%) −6.00 / in fixed budget; Retailer co-op (8%) + returns (4%) — / −1.68
Ex-factory product cost −3.50 / −3.50; Freight −0.55 / −0.75; Duty (15%) −0.53 / −0.53
Contribution per unit 4.73 / 7.55; Contribution margin 19.7% / 53.9%

claims.claim: Amazon contribution is very sensitive to ad cost
evidence: Each +1 pt of ACoS = −$0.24 per unit
ACoS 25% → $4.73 · 28% (pilot) → $4.01 · 32% (scale median) → $3.05 · 38% (top of range) → $1.61
Duty at 25% instead of 15% → −$0.35 per unit (Amazon $4.38; retail $7.20)

claims.claim: Retail doors cannot carry their own fixed cost
evidence: Per door: 4.5 units/week × 52 = 234 units × $7.55 = $1,766 contribution a year
Retail-only fixed cost: $6.0M national marketing + $1.5M field sales = $7.5M a year
Doors needed: $7.5M ÷ $1,766 ≈ 4,250, vs 600–1,000 in Option B

claims.claim: So retail only pays if it lifts Amazon sales, which is the halo assumption tested on slide 9

slides.title: Only the Amazon-led route stays within the board’s limits; retail-led breaches all three even on the planning team’s own inputs

claims.claim: Only Amazon-led stays within the limits; B breaches all three
evidence: Peak cash need ≤ $18M: A ✓ $1.9M; B ✗ $20.8M; J ✓ $1.1M
Group margin ≥ 8% every year: A ✓ min 9.5%; B ✗ 4.5% / 6.6% / 7.5% (2027–29); J ✓ min 10.1%
Revenue in 2030: A $26.4M (US); B $37.6M (US); J $7.0M (Japan)
Chart: cumulative cash end-2030 A +$2.4M, J +$1.8M, B −$20.8M vs investment cap −$18M

claims.claim: Why B fails: fixed cost, not unit margin
evidence: B carries $9.6M a year of fixed cost (A: $2.1M) plus $2.0M of 2027 one-offs (setup, launch fee, 600 × $1,100 fixtures).
2027 US operating loss of $8.7M takes group margin to (15.4 − 8.7) ÷ (140 + 11.3) = 4.5%.
B buys $11.2M more 2030 revenue than A for $23.2M more cash.

slides.title: Retail-led rests on inputs the evidence does not support: at Onsoo’s awareness, newcomers sell 2.6 units per door a week, below the 4.0 delisting line

claims.claim: Sell-through of 4.5 is a best case; most likely outcome: removal after the 12-month review
evidence: Median units/door/week by aided awareness: Below 10% 2.6; 10–20% 3.5; Above 20% 4.6; Option B assumes 4.5; delisting line 4.0
It comes from the retailer’s deck on successful newcomers and matches the median for brands with >20% awareness. Onsoo has 4%.
Even the top quartile of the below-10% group (3.4) falls short of 4.0; at 2.6 units and no halo, B’s peak cash need grows to $26.4M.

claims.claim: The 1.3× halo is a correlation, not a cause
evidence: Doors and Amazon sales correlate at 0.71 across 30 brands
Saebom added 300 doors after reaching ~$30M on Amazon
B would need a 3.1× halo to pay back by 2030
or 23.5 units per door a week instead of 4.5

claims.claim: The precedent is a loss of similar size
evidence: Mooncrest went retail-first in 450 doors in 2023, was removed in 2025 and lost an estimated $21M, close to B’s modeled −$20.8M.

slides.title: No route reaches $40M by 2030 within the limits: Amazon-led gets to ~$26M, and would reach $40M around 2032 if it keeps growing ~29% a year

claims.claim: Amazon-led gets to ~$26M and would reach $40M around 2032
evidence: A’s 2029→30 growth is 26.4 ÷ 20.4 − 1 = 29%. Held for two more years: $34M in 2031, $44M in 2032.

claims.claim: B gets closer ($37.6M) but burns $20.8M doing it, above the $18M cap
evidence: B’s 2030 revenue is $34.3M Amazon (1.43M units × $24) + $3.3M retail (234,000 units × $14).

claims.claim: Amazon-first can get there, but not always
evidence: Saebom (Amazon-first, 2022): ~$30M US revenue by 2025, then added 300 doors
Gaon Lab and Yeoreum (Amazon-first, 2022–23): both below $5M. Two of three stalled

claims.claim: Read “on the way to $40M by 2030” as a trajectory: “$25M+ by 2030, on a path to $40M by ~2032”
evidence: Hitting $40M by 2030 itself would mean relaxing the cash limits, and even B does not get there.

slides.title: Amazon-led pays back by 2030 only if ad cost averages ≤28.6% of sales, below the 32% median for brands at that scale

claims.claim: Breakeven ACoS is 28.6%
evidence: Planning case leaves +$2.40M at end-2030 on 2.81M units sold over 2027–30.
Each +1 pt ACoS costs $0.24 × 2.81M = $0.67M.
Breakeven = 25% + 2.40 ÷ 0.67 pts = 28.6%; with a 25% tariff from H2 2027: 27.0%.

claims.claim: Why 25% is unlikely to hold: the plan assumes ACoS falls as the brand matures; the evidence points the other way
evidence: Pilot: 28% on a small budget. Agency data for brands scaling $5–20M on Amazon: median 32% (range 26–38%), rising as brands bid on broader keywords.
A’s revenue is $7–26M in 2027–30, squarely in that band.

claims.claim: Volume matters less
evidence: At 25% ACoS payback survives a 21% volume shortfall; at 28% only a 4% shortfall.
Every cell keeps peak cash ≤$7.2M and group margin ≥8.8%.

slides.title: The downside is bounded: in every case tested, Amazon-led needs at most $7.2M of cash, 40% of the cap, and group margin stays above 8.8%

claims.claim: In every case tested, peak cash ≤$7.2M and group margin ≥8.8%
evidence: Planning case (ACoS 25%): peak $1.9M; end-2030 +$2.4M; min margin 9.5%; ✓ All met
Pilot ad cost (28%): $2.4M; +$0.4M; 9.3%; ✓ All met
Ramp to benchmark (28→30→32→32%): $2.7M; −$1.8M; 9.3%; ◐ Payback missed
Scale benchmark (32%): $3.2M; −$2.3M; 9.1%; ◐ Payback missed
Tariff rise (duty 25% from H2 2027, ACoS 25%): $2.1M; +$1.3M; 9.4%; ✓ All met
Benchmark + tariff: $3.8M; −$3.4M; 9.1%; ◐ Payback missed
Volume shortfall (70%, ACoS 28%): $3.2M; −$2.5M; 9.2%; ◐ Payback missed
Top of ACoS range (38%): $6.4M; −$6.4M; 8.8%; ◐ Payback missed
Stall like Gaon Lab / Yeoreum (flat 200k units, ACoS 32%): $7.1M; −$7.1M; 9.1%; ◐ Payback missed
Combined stress (ACoS 38%, 70% volume): $7.2M; −$7.2M; 8.9%; ◐ Payback missed
For comparison, Option B’s planning case needs $20.8M. Even the combined stress case for A uses 40% of the $18M cap

claims.claim: The risk in A is missing the 2030 payback, not breaching the cap or the margin floor.
evidence: Payback in the benchmark case: if units keep growing 20% a year after 2030, cumulative cash turns positive in 2032 (illustrative).

slides.title: Fund Amazon-led in gated stages, so the ad-cost question is answered on $2–3M of exposure before most of the money is spent

claims.claim: Stage 1 (Mar–Dec 2027): Build and prove ad cost at scale
evidence: US entity, MoCRA registration and safety substantiation, English labels (fixes the 6% complaint)
Four new SKUs; US team; $0.7M off-Amazon social budget aimed at TikTok, where 38% discover brands
2027 cost: $0.8M setup + $2.1M fixed; cash need $1.9–2.9M (ACoS 25–38%)

claims.claim: Gate 1 (Q1 2028 board): decide on H2-2027 data, at a $5–20M run-rate
evidence: Track monthly: ACoS, units vs 300k plan, 90-day repeat (29% today, 31% benchmark), tariff decision
Green: ACoS ≤28% and volume on plan → proceed to Stage 2 as planned; payback by 2030 holds
Amber: ACoS 28–34% → proceed, but freeze new fixed cost and no retail; payback slips to ~2031–32 with peak cash ≤$4.4M
Red: ACoS >34% or volume <70% of plan → cut back to core SKUs, re-plan, free the 2028 slot for Japan
If duty rises to 25%, lower each ACoS threshold by ~1.5 pts
34% ≈ the ACoS at which 2029 US operating profit is zero: ($10.73 − $2.1M ÷ 850k units) ÷ $24 = 34.4%

claims.claim: Stage 2 (2028–2029): Scale on Amazon; build awareness
evidence: Grow to 560k / 850k units; widen the range only where SKU-level economics match the hero product
Measure aided awareness among category buyers every six months
Gate 2 (2029): specialty retail is an option

claims.claim: Exposure at Gate 1 is the 2027 cash need of $1.9–2.9M, 11–16% of the $18M cap
evidence: If amber, peak cash stays ≤$4.4M; the red gate stops scaling before the $6–7M stress outcomes on slide 12.

slides.title: Specialty retail should be earned, not scheduled: raise the awareness trigger to 20% and prove 4.0 units per door in a test before any national roll-out

claims.claim: Amazon sales trigger > $10M (keep)
evidence: Reached in 2028 on plan ($13.4M)

claims.claim: Aided awareness trigger ≥ 20% among category buyers (vs CEO’s > 15%)
evidence: 4% today
At 10–20%, median sell-through is 3.5 units (IQR 2.8–4.3), below the 4.0 removal line; above 20% it is 4.6

claims.claim: Proof in store: 12-month test in a limited set of doors at ≥ 4.0 units/door/week
evidence: The retailer removes newcomers below 4.0 after 12 months; a test caps the Mooncrest-type loss

claims.claim: Halo: measured, not assumed 1.3×
evidence: The 0.71 correlation does not show cause

claims.claim: Cost base re-sized to the test; national budget only after the test
evidence: At $1,766 per door a year, 600–1,000 doors cover $1.1–1.8M, not $7.5M

claims.claim: Getting from 4% to 20% awareness is the real retail question
evidence: K-beauty buyers discover new brands on TikTok (38%) more than in stores (17%)
Saebom added 300 doors only after reaching ~$30M on Amazon

slides.title: Four uncertainties drive the result; ad cost matters most, and each has an early signpost and a planned response

claims.claim: 1 Ad cost at scale
evidence: Each +1 pt ACoS = −$0.67M; at the 32% median, −$2.3M (payback missed)
Signpost: monthly ACoS once run-rate passes $5M
Response: Gate 1 thresholds; shift spend to social/TikTok; favour SKUs with better repeat

claims.claim: 2 Volume and repeat
evidence: −15% volume: +$0.7M (still pays back); stall like Gaon Lab: −$7.1M
Signpost: units vs plan; 90-day repeat (29% vs 31% benchmark)
Response: US labels, new SKUs; red gate at <70% of plan

claims.claim: 3 Tariff 15% → 25%
evidence: −$0.35/unit; −$1.1M by 2030; breakeven ACoS 28.6% → 27.0%
Signpost: US decision, mid-2027
Response: re-run gates; consider price test (52% cite price as a reason to buy, so cautiously)

claims.claim: 4 FX (won)
evidence: 10% weaker won ≈ +$0.40/unit ≈ +$1.1M (if product cost is all in won)
Response: upside; set a hedging policy for the US cost base

slides.title: We ask the board to approve Stage 1 of the Amazon-led entry in March 2027 and to set the rules for the next two gates now

claims.claim: Approve US entry in 2027 via Option A, Amazon-led; reject the 600-door national retail launch (Option B); defer the Japan scale-up.
evidence: 2027 cash need $1.9–2.9M

claims.claim: Adopt Gate 1 thresholds for the Q1 2028 board: green ≤28% ACoS on plan volume; amber 28–34%; red >34% or volume <70% of plan.
evidence: Derived on slides 11 and 13

claims.claim: Pre-agree whether, in the amber case, a payback slip to ~2031–32 is acceptable while peak cash stays ≤$4.4M and group margin ≥9%. We recommend yes
evidence: the cap and floor hold, and Japan’s alternative adds only $1.8M
A departure from the 2030 payback limit: the board’s call

claims.claim: Restate the ambition as “$25M+ US revenue by 2030, on a path to $40M by ~2032”
evidence: no route reaches $40M by 2030 within the cash limits

claims.claim: Replace the retail trigger: Amazon sales >$10M and ≥20% aided awareness and a 12-month door test at ≥4.0 units/door/week.

slides.title: Option A (planning case): the US turns cash-positive in 2028 and pays back in 2030, with peak cash of $1.9M

claims.claim: Option A planning case pays back in 2030 with peak cash of $1.9M
evidence: Fixed and one-time cost: −2.90 / −2.10 / −2.10 / −2.10
US operating profit: −1.48 / 0.55 / 1.92 / 3.10
Group operating margin: 9.5% / 10.4% / 10.8% / 11.1%

claims.claim: At benchmark ACoS 32%, payback is missed
evidence: Contribution $3.045 per unit
US operating profit: −1.99 / −0.39 / 0.49 / 1.25

slides.title: Option B (planning case): fixed costs of $9.6M a year keep the US loss-making through 2030, and cash need peaks at $20.8M

claims.claim: Option B stays loss-making through 2030, cash need peaks at $20.8M
evidence: Amazon units (000): 390 / 728 / 1,105 / 1,430 (Option A × 1.3 halo)
Fixed cost: −9.60 each year ($2.1M as A + $6.0M retail marketing + $1.5M field sales)
US operating profit: −8.66 / −5.10 / −3.19 / −1.30
Group operating margin: 4.5% / 6.6% / 7.5% / 8.2%; below 8% in 2027, 2028 and 2029

claims.claim: What B would need to pay back by 2030: a 3.1× Amazon halo instead of 1.3×, or 23.5 units per door per week instead of 4.5
evidence: Its group margin stays below 8% in 2027 even then (5.6% at a 3× halo).

claims.claim: Realistic inputs (2.6 units/door/week, no halo): peak cash −$26.4M
evidence: If delisted after the 12-month review, the loss is cut, but peak cash still reaches −$10.1M in 2027 alone.

slides.title: Judgement calls we made where the briefing pack was ambiguous; each is flagged so the board can challenge it

claims.claim: “On the way to $40M by 2030” treated as a trajectory, not a hard 2030 test
evidence: If hard: no option passes; the board must relax cash limits or the target

claims.claim: Aided awareness among all category buyers used for Table 8: 4% (9% among K-beauty buyers)
evidence: None: both are below 10%, so the same 2.6 median applies

claims.claim: Inventory: year-end stock = 4/12 of the year’s landed cost; build is a cash outflow; no release by 2030
evidence: Lower stock would improve A and B similarly; ranking unchanged

claims.claim: Fixtures and launch fees expensed in the year incurred
evidence: Capitalising fixtures lifts B’s 2027 margin by <0.5 pt; still below 8%

claims.claim: Tariff: duty 20% blended in 2027 (25% from mid-year), 25% from 2028
evidence: Full-year 2027 at 25% costs a further ~$0.05M

claims.claim: Ex-US plan does not include the Japan scale-up: J is incremental to the $140–158M plan
evidence: If included, choosing the US removes J’s small profit (≤$1.3M a year) from the plan; conclusions unchanged

claims.claim: $3.6B skincare market size used, not the $5.2B trade-press figure
evidence: Market size does not constrain any option

normalized.recommendation: Approve US entry in 2027 via Option A, Amazon-led (Stage 1, 2027 cash need $1.9–2.9M); reject the 600-door national retail launch (Option B); defer the Japan scale-up. Adopt Gate 1 thresholds for the Q1 2028 board (green ≤28% ACoS on plan volume; amber 28–34%; red >34% or volume <70% of plan). Pre-agree whether, in the amber case, a payback slip to ~2031–32 is acceptable while peak cash stays ≤$4.4M and group margin ≥9% (we recommend yes). Restate the ambition as “$25M+ US revenue by 2030, on a path to $40M by ~2032”. Replace the retail trigger: Amazon sales >$10M and ≥20% aided awareness and a 12-month door test at ≥4.0 units/door/week.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Chosen: the only route that fits the board’s limits (peak cash $1.9M, payback 2030 +$2.4M, min group margin 9.5%); payback by 2030 holds only if ACoS ≤28.6%; to be funded in gated stages.

alternatives_considered.option: B · US Retail-led (600-door national retail launch plus Amazon)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: breaches all three limits even on its own inputs (−$20.8M peak cash vs $18M cap, no payback, 4.5% group margin in 2027); sell-through (4.5 vs 2.6 units/door/week) and 1.3× halo inputs are optimistic; Mooncrest precedent lost ~$21M.

Deferred: safer (+$1.8M cash by 2030, peak $1.1M, min margin 10.1%) but adds only $7M revenue in a market growing ~1.5% a year and does nothing for the US ambition; red gate would free the 2028 slot for Japan.

alternatives_considered.option: Waiting a year before US entry
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: would not resolve the key unknown, ad cost at scale, which can only be learned by scaling in the US; it would just delay the learning.

alternatives_considered.option: CEO’s retail trigger (add specialty retail from 2029 at >$10M Amazon sales and >15% awareness)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Does not hold: at 10–20% awareness median sell-through is 3.5 units/door/week, below the 4.0 delisting line; replaced by ≥20% awareness and a 12-month door test at ≥4.0.

alternatives_considered.option: Hitting $40M by 2030 as a hard target
alternatives_considered.treatment: Not adopted: no route reaches $40M by 2030 within the cash limits; would mean relaxing the cash limits, and even B does not get there.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Ad cost at scale: each +1 pt ACoS = −$0.67M; at the 32% median, −$2.3M (payback missed)
Volume and repeat: −15% volume: +$0.7M (still pays back); stall like Gaon Lab: −$7.1M
FX (won): 10% weaker won ≈ +$0.40/unit ≈ +$1.1M (if product cost is all in won)
Hero-product unit economics apply to all SKUs (planning-team convention); real SKU margins may differ.
Inventory = four months of landed cost (ex-factory + freight + duty), built up as volumes grow; not released by 2030.
All one-time costs, including in-store fixtures, expensed in the year incurred; no value counted beyond 2030.
Group margin = (ex-US plan at 11.0% + US operating profit) ÷ (ex-US plan revenue + US revenue); the ex-US plan excludes the Japan scale-up.
Japan (Option J) has no working-capital build (none given); this flatters J slightly.
300,000 units in 2027 assumes new SKUs sell like the first three.
The 1.3× halo is a correlation, not a cause.
“On the way to $40M by 2030” interpreted as a trajectory, not a hard 2030 test.
Aided awareness among all category buyers (4%) used for Table 8.
Tariff timing: duty 20% blended in 2027 (25% from mid-year), 25% from 2028.
$3.6B skincare market size used, not the $5.2B trade-press figure.
All figures come from the US-entry briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); KRW 1,380 per $.
